shots.visual_event: Door Eight becomes the 1913 control room as engineer Devika Rao turns the master clock back one fatal minute.
shots.dialogue_audio: Elias: “The minute saved thirteen bodies and duplicated thirteen lives.”

shots.visual_event: Two versions of the station overlap catastrophically—one intact, one wrecked—while people forget which families are theirs.
shots.dialogue_audio: Devika: “I saved them.” Station voice: “You divided them.”

shots.visual_event: Thirteen-year-old Nila understands first and steps onto the newborn train, clock-light cracking across her hands.
shots.dialogue_audio: Nila: “Take my life. Leave their memories.”

shots.visual_event: The two stations fuse safely; Nila becomes the living lock while Devika forgets she ever had a daughter.
Over a century, the train mechanizes the sacrifice, collecting replacements and storing unpaid memories behind twelve doors.
Elias shows what Nila omits: if she exits carrying all stored debt, every living citizen becomes a body without personal memory.
shots.dialogue_audio: Elias: “She can free the passengers—or leave a city of strangers.”

end_card.text: NILA IS NOT LYING — SHE IS DESPERATE
